title: Best AI Voice Agents for ENT (2026 Guide)
summary: Compare 5 AI voice agents for ENT and allergy practices. See which handle scheduling and the payer calls for prior auth and benefits checks.
body_markdown:
For ENT and allergy practices, the[best AI voice agent](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/healthcare-voice-ai-agents-guide) is the one that keeps working after the appointment is booked. Prosper AI is the only vendor in this comparison that handles patient calls (scheduling, intake, after-hours) and payer calls (benefits verification, prior auth follow-up) in one workflow. The other 4 cover the patient side and leave most payer work to staff.


Scheduling is the easy part. Prior auth follow-up, benefits checks, and billing calls are where most tools tap out, and your staff picks up the slack.


## **TL;DR**


- A booked appointment still has to be financially cleared, with coverage verified and prior auth approved before the patient arrives. Most AI voice agents for ENT and allergy practices stop at booking and leave that work to staff.
- Test every vendor on outbound payer calling, beyond inbound scheduling.
- Call flow architecture matters: rigid, pre-scripted flows hit a ceiling fast on the range of questions ENT and allergy callers ask.
- Prosper AI is the only vendor here that automates patient-facing and payer-facing calls in one workflow.
- Prosper AI resolves 60%+ of inbound call volume end-to-end in production, with two-stage insurance verification and 80+ EHR integrations


## What are AI voice agents for ENT and allergy practices?


AI voice agents for[ENT and allergy practices](https://www.getprosper.ai/outpatient-groups/ent) are healthcare voice AI agents that handle inbound and outbound calls for scheduling, insurance verification, prior authorization follow-up, billing questions, and after-hours coverage, then write each outcome back to the EHR. They hold natural, multi-turn conversations, so a patient can switch from rescheduling to a coverage question mid-call without getting transferred.


ENT call volume spans surgical scheduling, audiology, allergy testing, and recurring immunotherapy visits. A voice agent works as an always-on extension of the front office, so staff can spend their time on the calls that need a person.


## How we ranked AI voice agents for ENT and allergy practices


We ranked each vendor on how much of an ENT and allergy practice's phone work it can finish without staff, from booking the visit to clearing it with the payer. That scope matters because prior auth is a daily workload. According to[AMA](https://www.ama-assn.org/press-center/ama-press-releases/ama-survey-prior-authorization-reform-pledge-falls-short-physicians) , physicians complete an average of 40 prior authorizations per week, which eats up about 13 hours of physician and staff time. Each manual prior auth[costs specialists $15.12](https://www.caqh.org/hubfs/CAQH%20Insights_2023%20Index%20Report_Provider%20Specialty%20Issue%20Brief_Final.pdf) , versus $6.61 electronically.


ENT procedures like tonsillectomies, septoplasties, sinus surgeries, and audiology diagnostics routinely need prior auth, and allergy practices add biologic and immunotherapy authorizations on top. Here are the criteria we used:


- EHR integration with native read-and-write access, so outcomes land in the chart
- Call mix coverage beyond scheduling, including billing inquiries, benefits verification, and prior authorization workflows
- Architecture generation: scripted state machines cap out quickly on ENT's intent variance; LLM-native systems handle it better
- Outbound payer-calling capability for prior auth follow-up without staff involvement
- After-hours and multilingual call handling included as standard
- Time-to-live and ongoing workflow customization support


A vendor that only handles scheduling leaves payer calls, benefits checks, and billing questions on your staff's plate.

Prosper AI is a healthcare-native AI workforce of voice agents built to cover the full administrative call surface, from inbound scheduling through outbound payer calls, without splitting the workflow across multiple vendors. Here is what that looks like in practice:

Prosper AI is the only option in this comparison that automates both patient-facing and payer-facing calls within a single workflow, making it the strongest fit for ENT practices vetting voice AI for healthcare front-desk automation with high procedure volume and complex payer requirements.


## Assort Health


Assort Health is a patient-facing AI voice agent for specialty scheduling. It raised a $120M Series C in June 2026. Using a scripted agentic state machine, the architecture is deterministic and auditable, which works well when call flows are narrow and predictable.


What they offer:


- Inbound scheduling and rescheduling for new and existing patients
- Hundreds of hand-encoded specialty call-flow nodes
- Multilingual support via parallel call trees


For ENT practices with stable, narrow scheduling workflows, Assort is functional. The limitations show up fast in higher-complexity settings: eligibility is handled through a post-call web form instead of real-time in-call verification and expanding to new call types after go-live requires vendor engineering instead of self-configuration. ENT practices with routine prior authorization for sinus surgeries or audiology diagnostics will likely hit that ceiling within the first few months.


## Hyro


Over $95M raised and deployed across 45+ health systems (per Hyro), Hyro is purpose-built for large health system scale. It handles patient-facing conversations well, particularly where Epic integration and multi-channel reach matter.


What they offer:


- Inbound scheduling, FAQ answering, and provider search across voice, chat, and SMS
- HIPAA-compliant EHR and EMR integrations, including a listing in the Epic Showroom
- Multi-channel patient engagement including web chat and SMS alongside voice


Hyro is a reasonable fit for large health systems that need patient-facing call containment at scale. The gap for ENT practices is payer-side coverage: Hyro handles patient-facing interactions but does not automate outbound calls to insurance payers for prior authorization, benefits verification, or claims follow-up. For an independent or PE-backed ENT and allergy group where surgical prior auth for tonsillectomies or sinus procedures generates daily call volume, that gap is hard to work around.


## Parakeet Health


Parakeet Health launched in October 2024 with a generative AI voice agent focused on patient engagement, securing $3 million in seed funding led by Canvas Ventures.


What they offer:


- Inbound scheduling, rescheduling, and cancellation handling via direct EHR integration
- Proactive outbound calls for referral follow-up, post-discharge check-ins, and care gap closure
- Appointment backfilling through outbound outreach campaigns


For ENT practices researching[voice AI use cases for specialty clinics](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/use-cases-for-voice-ai-in-outpatient-specialty-clinics) and wanting to automate outbound patient engagement alongside basic scheduling, Parakeet is worth considering. Publicly available information does not document real-time in-call insurance verification, outbound payer calls for prior authorization, or billing call automation. ENT surgical workflows, where tonsillectomy and sinus procedure prior auth drives daily volume, need that payer-facing capability built in. Practices with complex prior authorization requirements will likely find the coverage gap too wide.


## Hello Patient


Hello Patient is a generative AI voice agent purpose-built for outpatient medical practices, handling scheduling, intake, and after-hours coverage through an AI agent named Mia. It raised $22.5 million in Series A funding and now powers 10,000 to 20,000 provider-patient conversations per day.


What they offer:


- Inbound and after-hours call handling via Mia across voice, text, and chat
- Two-way text confirmations and digital intake forms
- Appointment scheduling, rescheduling, and cancellation management


For smaller ENT practices researching[AI voice agents in healthcare](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/ai-voice-agent-in-healthcare-guide-use-cases) that need multi-channel patient communication without a heavy implementation lift, Hello Patient is a credible option. The constraint is payer-side coverage: insurance verification, prior authorization calls, and billing automation.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### **How do I choose the right AI voice agent for an ENT practice with high surgical volume?**


Start by mapping your full call mix, not merely scheduling volume. ENT practices with routine prior authorization for sinus surgeries, septoplasties, and tonsillectomies need a vendor that covers outbound payer calls and in-call insurance verification, beyond appointment booking. Any vendor that hands payer-side workflows back to staff is automating less than half the problem.


### **Are AI voice agents for ENT practices HIPAA compliant?**


They can be, if the vendor signs a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and holds independent security certification like SOC 2 Type II. Ask for both before any patient call data flows. Prosper AI signs a BAA with every customer and is SOC 2 Type II certified.


### **What should I ask a vendor before committing to an AI voice agent for my ENT practice?**


Ask directly whether the tool writes outcomes back to your EHR, handles outbound calls to insurance payers for prior authorization without staff involvement, and covers billing inquiries in addition to scheduling. Then call a live customer number and test whether the agent handles an off-script insurance question or a mid-call topic change without transferring.


### **When does an ENT practice need a generative AI voice agent versus a scripted one?**


A scripted system works when call flows are narrow, stable, and predictable. ENT practices with mixed surgical and audiology scheduling, complex payer requirements, and billing inquiries generate enough intent variance that scripted architectures quickly hit their coverage ceiling. Generative systems handle mid-call topic changes, off-script questions, and multi-step payer interactions that scripted state machines require vendor engineering to support.


### **Can AI voice agents handle allergy workflows like immunotherapy scheduling?**


Yes, if the agent can follow your rules for allergy testing, recurring immunotherapy injections, and biologic follow-ups. Allergy practices should also test payer-side coverage, since biologics for asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps usually need prior authorization. Prosper AI learns practice-specific appointment rules during implementation and handles the payer calls tied to them.


### **How long does it take to implement an AI voice agent in an ENT practice?**


Published go-live timelines range from about 3 weeks to several months. Prosper AI goes live in 3 weeks with no custom coding. Assort Health reports an average of 7 weeks from data access, and Hello Patient says most clients go live in about 6 weeks.
